content.title: Reach the sales contact page from a homepage Contact sales control
content.intent: Prove that the anonymous visitor can use a visible homepage Contact sales control to open the sales contact page and reach the rendered sales form.
content.technique_notes: Applied the Web form profile because the journey ends on a public data-entry form and the source limits coverage to render and validation without submission. Applied equivalence partitioning to treat visible homepage Contact sales controls as one successful-navigation family because the required outcome is unchanged by control location. Negative, boundary-value, and covering-array techniques were not applied here because this path proves navigation and rendered form presence rather than constrained input combinations.

content.title: Show inline validation for empty required sales-form input
content.intent: Prove that leaving required sales-form input empty triggers inline validation on the sales form without completing a real lead submission.
content.technique_notes: Applied the Web form profile and negative/error technique because the source explicitly requires client-side validation on the unauthenticated form. Applied equivalence partitioning over empty-like invalid input using the source's suggested synthetic values such as an empty string and a single space; these stay as parameter variation because they should produce the same validation outcome. Boundary-value analysis and covering-array generation were not applied because the evidence gives invalid classes, not numeric or length bounds for this sales-form promise.

content.title: Show inline validation for malformed sales-form input
content.intent: Prove that malformed input on a format-constrained sales-form field triggers inline validation on the sales form without completing a real lead submission.
content.technique_notes: Applied the Web form profile and negative/error technique because the source explicitly requires malformed-input validation on the unauthenticated sales form. Applied equivalence partitioning to keep multiple malformed examples in one scenario because they should produce the same validation outcome; I used the owner-approved generic malformed rule rather than inventing an exact field or message that the corpus does not name. Boundary-value analysis and covering-array generation were not applied because the malformed-input promise is expressed as a single validation family, not as bounded numeric input or a cross-field combination problem.

judgements.rationale: [applicability] Applied Web form profile, equivalence partitioning, and negative/error techniques because the use-case is a public website form journey limited to rendering and client-side validation. Did not apply auth because the source states anonymous execution only; did not apply API-contract because the promised surface is the rendered website, not an endpoint; did not apply state-flow because the evidence does not describe a multi-step wizard; did not apply CRUD, idempotency, concurrency, or notification because no submission or persisted side effect is allowed; did not apply mobile-native because the source names the web application under test as https://www.twilio.com/en-us.
